newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia tax office denies A$640 mln shortfall.
newsitem.headline: Australia tax office denies A$640 mln shortfall.

text.p: Australia's Tax Office on Wednesday denied a newspaper report that the government faced a budget shortfall through lower small business tax collection.
Tax Commissioner Michael Carmody said in a statement that rather than the A$640 million shortfall reported by the Australian Financial Review, collections were running ahead of projections.

"There is no shortfall. In fact, overall company tax collections are, at this stage, some A$200 million ahead of the mid-year forecast, with small business tax collections estimated to be ahead by A$150 million," he said.
"The ... article draws on a Tax Office document that illustrates the effect of shifting collections to relieve the burden on small business of lodging tax returns," Carmody said.
"The shift in payment schedules has no effect on revenue."
The newspaper, citing a February Tax Office internal document, on Wednesday reported an expected A$640 million shorfall in 1996/97 shortfall, saying it had prompted a crackdown on small business.
Carmody confirmed authorities had identified some areas of "compliance risk" and taken steps to combat that.
Australia's budget for the fiscal year to June 30, 1997, is expected to produce an underlying deficit -- excluding asset sales and state government debt repayments -- of A$8.5 billion.
Treasurer Peter Costello is due to announce the 1997/98 budget on May 13.
